card: Removes noexcept from LogOversizedDbCache so invalid dbcache settings fail with an error instead of aborting the process. When settings.json contains a non-integer or out-of-range dbcache value (e.g. 4096.5), GetIntArg throws std::runtime_error, which hit the noexcept boundary and caused std::terminate to abort bitcoind during startup. Removing noexcept allows AppInit to catch the exception and exit cleanly with status 1 and an error message.
changed_since_previous: No changes to the patch; this update provides the diff.
evidence: PR description notes the abort crash during startup: 'libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type std::runtime_error: JSON integer out of range'
The PR includes a functional test in `test/functional/feature_settings.py` reproducing the issue with `{"dbcache": 4096.5}` and asserting that `AppInit` catches the exception.
problem: `LogOversizedDbCache` calls `CalculateDbCacheBytes` which calls `GetIntArg`. If `settings.json` contains a non-integer or out-of-range integer for `dbcache` (such as `4096.5`), `GetIntArg` throws a `std::runtime_error`; because `LogOversizedDbCache` was marked `noexcept`, the exception triggers an immediate `std::terminate` abort during startup instead of being caught by the `AppInit` exception handler.

risk.why: Only removes a noexcept qualification to allow an existing startup exception to propagate to the main exception handler.

summary: Removes the `noexcept` specifier from `LogOversizedDbCache` so exceptions thrown during cache size calculations can propagate to `AppInit`. This prevents `bitcoind` from aborting via `std::terminate` when `settings.json` contains a malformed `-dbcache` value, allowing it to exit cleanly with an error message instead.
